key_insight: Supersonic HV-APS with axial powder feeding produces denser, harder Cr3C2–NiCr coatings than conventional APS, but this does not translate into better erosion resistance at 90° impact.
engineering_relevance: For wear-critical coatings, axial-feed HV-APS can meaningfully improve tribological performance and microstructural quality, making it a strong alternative to standard APS for demanding surface protection.
method: APS with radial powder injection using a single-electrode A60 torch
HV-APS with axial powder feeding using a three-electrode Axial III torch
Compared porosity, phase composition, microhardness, erosion, and ball-on-disc wear on Cr3C2–NiCr coatings on S235 steel
evidence_signal: HV-APS cut porosity from 11.99% to 6.16% and increased hardness from 897 to 1141 HV0.2, while reducing wear volume from 3.90 to 2.85 mm3; erosion rates stayed nearly the same (0.20 vs 0.19 mg/g).
watch_item: The improved density and hardness did not improve erosion performance at high impact angle, so process choice should be matched to the dominant wear mode.
paper_title: Microstructure and wear properties of Cr₃C₂–NiCr coatings sprayed by conventional and supersonic high-velocity atmospheric plasma spraying with axial powder feeding
